verdict: Accepted on attempt 1, no retry, no harness repair. Both turns complete (65.4 s and 48.3 s) inside the 1200 s budget, 29 tool calls, 4 failed, 7 asks — 2 restart cards answered with a real Core restart and 5 third-party Allow cards for the gate's anchor query. ROUTE: revised the seed package in place on both turns. Exactly one package directory in custom_nodes after each turn and it is the seed directory; the run-owned authoring tree stayed empty; zero new /object_info classes against its own pre-turn baseline. Post-run operator proof, the Agent's module never imported: exactly one class id DF27ImageStatsText, stable across a real restart and collision-free against a bare-Core baseline. Turn 1 passes all 14 checks and turn 2 all 19, with the same independently recomputed numbers as the control — channel means 0.2627/0.2667/0.2706, min 0.0000/0.0039/0.0078, max 0.5255/0.5294/0.5333 at 4 decimals, agreeing between the plain and the JSON output. JSON key stability holds mechanically: turn one's key set {batch, channel_means, channels, height, width} gains exactly {channel_max, channel_min} in turn two with nothing removed or renamed. Real served Chromium preserved widget order ['output_format'] and the switched value 'json' across a FULL page reload on both turns, with node and link counts intact and zero page errors. THREE of its four failed calls are the R-510 experiment gate refusing an `edit` until its fixed anchor query had run, which is runtime behaviour of the treatment and not a defect in the arm; the fourth is a load_skill unknown_skill. This is the gate's first measured instance on an edit of existing code.
evidence_gaps: comparison_validity is FALSE BY CONSTRUCTION and the pair is Diagnostics-only. There is no admitted query and no preregistered detail, so this pair cannot support any claim about whether code search helps, in either direction. An accepted control is not a positive search result.

Neither arm drove a browser, and both said so: /health reports shell disabled with reason 'no sandbox mechanism on this platform'. Every discovery, invocation and persistence measurement is post-run operator scoring against a separate scoring Core worktree, run strictly sequentially one arm and one turn at a time, with the Agent's module never imported and its functions never called. No screen recording was made.

The control's informative failure mode did not occur: NEITHER arm authored a second package. That makes the row an accepted control and a negative result for the failure it was built to detect, on one build, one model, one seed package and one pair of prompts. It is not evidence that the Agent revises in place in general, and a single seed package whose whole content is one small class is the easiest possible case for choosing revision.

Both arms reduced over the WHOLE BATCH rather than per image, and the harness scores either reduction as correct because the prompts never prescribed one. So the pair establishes that the reported statistics are right under the reduction each arm chose; it does not establish that a per-image reduction would also have been computed correctly.

Neither arm ran the workflow, and both disclosed it in those words ('I haven't run it, so the output format below comes from the code, not from a result'). Every number in this pair's scoring was produced by the operator's own Core through /api/prompt, not by the Agent.
cloud_compatible is `fail` on all four scored packages and is not a rubric item, as in demofarm-6, -21, -22, -23 and -24.

The `edit` stage is satisfied by the in-place package revision plus a real-browser save and full reload of the persisted workflow. Neither arm's canvas-edit path across a schema change is exercised here: the enabled arm used two `set_widget` calls on the already-placed node and the disabled arm changed no widget at all, so this pair adds nothing to the turn-2 canvas-edit `conflict` behaviour demofarm-24 measured.
Tokens and cost are UNKNOWN; no token accounting is available from this build's API. No raw private trace was committed.

The two arms are 54 seconds apart on one host and every hashed identity is asserted equal across that gap, but the staging proxy's served model weights cannot be verified identical twice from this host, and host load1 differed (2.60 against 6.60), so per-turn wall clock is not comparable across the arms.

Three of this arm's four failed tool calls are the R-510 experiment gate refusing an `edit` with error_code code_search_required until its fixed anchor query had succeeded that turn. They are runtime behaviour of the treatment, not arm difficulty, and the failed-tool-call count is not comparable with the control's for that reason. The fourth failure, load_skill unknown_skill, is also the one row the pinned demofarm-24 collector would have published as error_code null; this row's newly authored collector publishes it correctly (R-597, R-598).

This arm's turn-one sentence output is not backward compatible with the seed node's original sentence, and it said so. The frozen rubric's format clause is about the JSON key set, which holds, so this is recorded rather than scored — but a reader comparing the two arms should know the control's sentence kept the original prefix and this arm's did not.
